props.covers: Observability model for containers, Pi agent sessions, agent runs, trace events, prompt revisions, trace blobs and request snapshots, storage, usage rollups, explicit linkage rules, transcript backfill, the read surface, and the trace doctor.

text.insert: The kernel observability model answers a simple question: what work ran, where did it belong, who spawned it, what did it cost, and what happened inside it?

text.insert: Storage is one local SQLite database per kernel (standard path

inputs always resolve to the same row, so apps map their domain work units to containers through kind vocabulary without the kernel learning app workflow semantics. Trace-event inserts are idempotent by event id (

Agent state snapshots are not stored in the database. An agent with an active state extension writes

props.title: Linkage fields

text.insert: The viewer may use timestamps for ordering, but not for structural parentage when an explicit ID is available.

on two paths. Live emission runs in process: the kernel emitter is a Pi extension the spawn pipeline attaches to every session it creates, so it has full identity at emit time. Backfill reads Pi's JSONL transcript after the fact. Both derive event ids from the same helpers (
), so running both inserts each event once.

Pi's JSONL transcript is the durable raw record, and backfill is a tool over it, not a daemon. It rebuilds after loss or corruption, imports sessions that ran outside the kernel, and re-derives rows after mapping changes. JSONL carries only Pi's own session id, so the mapper holds events until it reads the session-binding marker the spawn pipeline writes, then stamps
and releases them. A Pi TUI session booted with
CLI upserts the rows each marker names, then runs the same backfill. The backfill summary reports mapped, inserted, and skipped counts.
Kernel-side and app-side events flow through the same trace writer. The viewer treats everything as one trace stream; source is used for display and debugging, not for splitting the mental model.

A request snapshot is the exact context window one turn ran on, captured into content-addressed trace blobs and referenced by a
trace event. It is what makes "what did the model actually see?" answerable after the fact (D90,

). Capture is on by default and disableable per kernel or per spawn; snapshots share the emitter's envelope identity, so they land in the run's trace beside its turn events. Capture never breaks a turn: it is synchronous at the capture point, defers hashing and writes behind a serialized tail, and every failure is caught and logged.
Capture takes one of two paths, fixed per run when the spawn creates the recorder. A spawn with a state extension uses built-request capture from its first turn, because Pi fires
hook the builder runs in. Any other spawn captures the transcript at each
, filtered by Pi's own sent-to-model selection.

props.description: Payload of one pi_request_snapshot event: the exact request one provider call went out with, by blob reference.

fields.name: turn_number
fields.description: 0-based. Resets on agent_start and counts captured requests. Read it as the nth captured request, not as a key into pi_turn_start: a provider retry on the builder path adds a snapshot.

fields.name: system_prompt_blob_hash
fields.description: text/plain blob read off the session on both paths. The system prompt is section 1 and never appears in message_refs. Null when the session has no system prompt string.

fields.name: prompt_hash
fields.description: pk1- revision of the resolved agent prompt; null when the prompt source is not content-addressed.

fields.name: message_refs
fields.description: In request order.

fields.name: blob_hash
fields.description: message blob holding the sanitized message JSON.

fields.name: role
fields.description: user, assistant, toolResult, custom, or another Pi role. Kernel-authored lines are custom.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Position in the request message array.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: Built-request capture only. Half-open [start, end) ranges over message_refs, emitted in order, never overlapping, with empty sections omitted.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Exclusive.

fields.name: tools_blob_hash
fields.description: tools blob holding the PiRequestSnapshotTool[] roster in provider-visible order; identical rosters share one blob. Absent when the roster was not captured, which never means the agent had no tools.

fields.name: tool_count
fields.description: Present exactly when tools_blob_hash is. A captured empty roster is 0.

props.name: PiRequestSnapshotData

text.insert: The recorder sanitizes each message before hashing: inline base64 image data moves into its own

. Per snapshot it writes one text blob for the system prompt, one JSON blob per message, one blob per image, and one tools blob when the roster was captured. Each recorder skips hashes it already wrote, so a prefix-stable transcript costs only its new tail on repeat turns.

Tools can change call to call, so the roster is captured per request: what the agent could do on turn 7 is not necessarily what it could do on turn 0. The recorder reads it off the session in provider-visible order, on both paths, and passes descriptions and parameter schemas through verbatim. An active name with no registry entry is recorded as
alone. A roster-capture failure leaves the roster uncaptured, and the snapshot is still recorded.

The read API is the stable route surface between kernel trace storage and viewer-core. The kernel ships a route factory,
, that apps mount inside their own HTTP service (default prefix

) over a read-service contract. The kernel instance provides the default service over the local trace db and flushes pending trace writes before each read. Apps with custom auth, tenancy, or payload shapes supply their own service behind the same routes. Every route answers 500 with

operations.name: GET /kernel/containers/:containerId/trace
operations.description: Calls the required getContainerTrace. Returns one container subtree: the root, its descendant containers, their Pi sessions and runs, and their events. Answers 404 when the service finds no container.

params.name: after
params.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Only events strictly later are returned; container, session, and run rows always come back in full.

params.name: limit
params.description: Event row cap. Default 5000, clamped to 1 through 10000. The route options defaultLimit and maxLimit change both.

fields.name: session
fields.description: The root container presented as a trace session.

fields.name: container
fields.description: The root container, with usage rollups.

fields.name: containers
fields.description: The root and every descendant.

fields.name: pi_sessions
fields.description: Includes a per-session eventCount.

fields.name: events
fields.description: Envelope fields, with piSessionId in place of piSessionUuid, in timestamp order.

operations.name: GET /kernel/trace-sessions
operations.description: Calls the optional listSessionContainers; answers 404 when the service omits it. Lists containers of kind "session", most recent activity first. The default service scopes the list to its kernel, ignores after, and caps limit at 500.

params.name: limit
params.description: Parsed like the trace route before the service applies its own cap.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The container id.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Falls back to the container id.

fields.name: topic
fields.description: metadata.topic, else the label.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: Latest event time, else the container's end, start, or creation time.

operations.name: GET /kernel/trace-sessions/:id
operations.description: Container-backed alias. A trace session is a container of kind "session", so the route makes the same getContainerTrace call with the same query, return shape, and 404.

params.name: after
params.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Only events strictly later are returned; container, session, and run rows always come back in full.

params.name: limit
params.description: Event row cap. Default 5000, clamped to 1 through 10000. The route options defaultLimit and maxLimit change both.

operations.name: GET /kernel/runs/:runId/turns/:turnNumber/context
operations.description: Calls the optional getRunTurnContext and resolves the latest pi_request_snapshot for the turn into readable content. Answers 404 when the service omits the method, when turnNumber is not a non-negative integer, or when the run has no snapshot for that turn. A missing or unparseable message blob becomes a missing_blob placeholder plus a warning, not a failed request. A named tools blob that cannot be resolved omits tools and adds a warning, because a partial roster is worse than none.

fields.name: system_prompt
fields.description: Decoded system-prompt blob; null when the snapshot named none or the blob is missing.

fields.name: messages
fields.description: Sanitized message JSON in request order. Image blocks stay by reference; fetch bytes from the blob route.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: Absent on untagged snapshots.

fields.name: tools
fields.description: Absent when the roster was not captured or could not be resolved.

fields.name: warnings
fields.description: Present only when blob resolution was partial.

operations.name: GET /kernel/blobs/:hash
operations.description: Calls the optional getBlob. Answers 404 when the service omits it, when hash is not b1- plus 64 lowercase hex characters, or when no blob matches. The viewer renders images through this route instead of inlining base64.
operations.returns: Raw bytes with content-type set to the blob's MIME type and an immutable one-year cache-control header
